the identification of priority areas for Opuntia species conservation and the establishment of a multi-criteria approach to conservation planning that is applicable to a variety of species and landscapes.
the identification of priority areas for conserving biodiversity in multi-use landscapes.
the design of a conservation area network for Opuntia species in México, which can be used as a model to address conservation planning for other plant groups and regions of the world.

we have identified a set of large, contiguous, and well–connected areas in México that can be managed for the conservation of biodiversity in Opuntia cactus species.

Opuntia conservation is best achieved through the sustainable management of large areas, not through traditional land reservation, and that multi-criteria analysis can be a useful tool for devising implementable plans for this.
